description: Narrowed PI error pipeline from 16-bit to 1-bit (sign only) across stages 2-3, since anti-windup only uses the error sign bit — saves 30 FFs per PI instance (60 total).

Removed 8 x 16-bit debug latch registers (128 FFs) from foc_top — submodule outputs are already registered and hold their values between FOC iterations, so Wishbone debug reads now go directly to the datapath wires.

Removed 2x16-bit `stored_sin`/`stored_cos` latch registers (32 FFs) from foc_top — CORDIC output registers already hold sin/cos values stable between iterations, so Park and Inverse Park now read directly from the CORDIC outputs.

Removed 3×10-bit `reg_duty_a/b/c` latch registers (30 FFs) from foc_top — SVPWM output registers already hold duty values stable between FOC iterations, so output pins and Wishbone debug reads now go directly to the SVPWM outputs.

Removed redundant input-delay registers `ia_d1` (16 FFs) from Clarke and `va_s1` (16 FFs) from SVPWM — inputs are stable during submodule execution since the FSM serializes all operations, so stage 2 can read the module inputs directly without a pipeline delay copy.

Removed the 16-bit `i_alpha` output register from Clarke stage 2 — since `i_alpha = ia` (Clarke identity) and `ia` comes from `reg_ia` which is a stable Wishbone register, the value is always valid without needing a pipeline register. Park reads it only after Clarke completes, so timing is preserved. Saves 16 FFs.

Removed `u_p_s3` (16-bit) and `error_sign_s3` (1-bit) pipeline registers from PI controller stage 3 — stage 2 registers (`u_p_s2`, `error_sign_s2`) are stable when stage 4 fires because the FSM serializes PI execution, so no re-latching is needed. Saves 17 FFs per PI instance (34 FFs total across D and Q axes).

Removed `cos_val`/`sin_val` output registers (32 FFs) from CORDIC — `x_reg`, `y_reg`, and `quad_reg` are stable from CORDIC completion through Park and Inverse Park execution, so post-correction outputs can be combinational.

Removed redundant two-level accumulator clamping in PI controller stage 3 — `int_max_ext` (max 30 bits) is always within the 32-bit accumulator range, so the intermediate `clamp_acc` against ACC_MAX/ACC_MIN was dead logic. Eliminating it saves 4×33-bit comparators across both PI instances.

Restructured SVPWM min/max to share 3 signed comparators between both computations instead of using 6 separate ones — saves 3×16-bit comparator/subtractor circuits while producing identical results (equal-value tie-breaking doesn't affect vmax/vmin values).

Removed 3×16-bit pipeline registers (`va_s2`, `vb_s2`, `vc_s2` = 48 FFs) from SVPWM stage 2 — inputs `v_alpha`, `vb_s1`, `vc_s1` are stable registered values during SVPWM execution, so min/max/offset and phase adjustment can be computed combinationally in stage 3 without intermediate registering.

Merged duplicate output-clamp comparators with anti-windup saturation detection in PI controller stage 4 — `saturated` flag now derived from the same if/else that computes `out_clamped`, eliminating 2×17-bit redundant comparators per PI instance (4 comparators total across D and Q axes).

Replaced full-width signed constant comparisons with 1-bit XOR overflow detection across all 6 datapath modules (CORDIC `saturate`, Clarke/Park/InvPark `sat_add`, PI `clamp_dw`, SVPWM `sqrt3_mul`). This replaces pairs of multi-bit magnitude comparators with single-bit sign-mismatch checks — functionally identical but synthesizes to smaller logic since `val[N] != val[N-1]` is a 1-bit XOR vs two (N+1)-bit comparisons against constants.

Reduced CORDIC `iter` counter from 5 bits to 4 bits (`$clog2(16)=4` vs `$clog2(17)=5`) — iter only needs values 0–15, so the extra bit was wasted. This removes one mux level from both 16-bit barrel shifters (`x_reg >>> iter`, `y_reg >>> iter`) and saves 1 FF, reducing area and shortening the critical path through the shifters.

Replaced 3 SVPWM PWM-scaling multipliers (`v * 1023`) with shift-subtract (`(v << 10) - v`) — since `PWM_MAX = 2^PWM_BITS - 1`, the multiply by constant `1023` decomposes exactly into a shift and subtract, eliminating three 16×11-bit multipliers in favor of three 26-bit subtractors.

Replaced the Clarke transform's 16×16 constant multiplier (`sum_stage * INV_SQRT3`) with an equivalent 6-term shift-add chain, since INV_SQRT3 = 18919 = 2^14 + 2^11 + 2^9 - 2^5 + 2^3 - 2^0. This is algebraically identical (produces the exact same product for all inputs) but eliminates one hardware multiplier in favor of shifts and adders, reducing area similarly to experiment 15's SVPWM multiplier elimination.

Replaced the Clarke transform's 16×16 constant multiplier (`sum_stage * INV_SQRT3`) with a 6-term CSD shift-add chain (18919 = 2^14 + 2^11 + 2^9 - 2^5 + 2^3 - 2^0), eliminating one hardware multiplier in favor of shifts and adders to reduce area.

**Summary:** Merged Park and Inverse Park transforms into a single shared `foc_rotate` module — they never execute concurrently (sequential FSM states), so sharing eliminates 4 of 8 16x16 multipliers plus duplicate pipeline registers, sat_add, and sat_neg logic, with only minimal mux overhead for input/mode selection.
